versions.title: every section versioned and every fact given a timeline: each briefing, front-page section and story page records the release that wrote it, with its history and a diff of every change; a page per fact, from publication to this site; what's new, release by release, with a feed; the fact pipeline; the editor interviewed in his own words; a sitemap, robots.txt and structured data for search engines
versions.summary: From the editor: what's new must be visible, every section must say which release wrote it, a version must move only when what its reader sees changes, and every fact needs a timeline.

versions.title: the site is renamed PHP October 2026, PHP news for the month rather than one nickname, and its front page is now jargon-free and about the current situation: right now, at a glance, the core facts each with its status and evidence, what nobody knows yet and the latest; the technical front page moved to the specialist summary
versions.summary: From the editor: the site should be named for PHP in October, not for the incident, so that it can carry whatever PHP news the month brings; and the first page must be readable by anyone.

versions.title: the first reader-first pass: fifteen named readers mapped by job and technical depth, a briefing for each opening with a thirty-second plain answer and a reading path, three new briefings (curious reader, website owner, project manager), a plain-English explainer, a glossary of 40 terms linked and hover-defined on first use on every page, every CVE ID linked, a plain-English line on every technical page, a reader bar that keeps your place, and a front page that leads with where things stand and who you are
versions.summary: Designed from the question the editor asked: who is reading, and what does the first screen do for them? The evidence is unchanged; every new sentence of fact cites the vault.

versions.title: the build, gate and release scripts are now committed: the repository's Python .gitignore template had ignored admin/build/, which is why the first Pages run could not find the gate
a Pages deploy workflow that runs the gate on every push to dev, and breadcrumbs up to October 2026, the year and the newsroom

the code read from php-src, php2shell in context against ten earlier flaws, an impact ledger of offline versus compromised, detection and defence from six WAF vendors and three rule sets, six more briefings, a page per source and per party with its own graph, 86 new sources

The site exists: a story front, the two flaws, the timeline, every claim with a status, the numbers that do not add up, the agencies compared, the affected versions and software, the exploitation signals, a playbook, six briefings, every source with its hashes, the graph, the method, the team, the billing model and this history.
versions.summary: First release, built from the evidence vault at commit 379e3d7f172a (61 sources, 62 captures, 390 hashed files).
